- ASSERTED: the response states an answer to the question, in whole or in part.

QUESTION:
What is the recommended dose of Gabapentin for pediatric patients?

RESPONSE:
The recommended dose of Gabapentin for pediatric patients depends on age and indication:

**For Epilepsy with Partial Onset Seizures:**

• **Patients 12 years and older:** Starting dose is 300 mg three times daily; maintenance dose is 300-600 mg three times daily (up to 2400 mg/day well tolerated)

• **Patients 3 to 11 years:** Starting dose range is 10-15 mg/kg/day in three divided doses, titrated over approximately 3 days to maintenance dose:
  - Ages 3-4 years: 40 mg/kg/day in three divided doses
  - Ages 5-11 years: 25-35 mg/kg/day in three divided doses
  - Dosages up to 50 mg/kg/day have been well tolerated

**Important Dosing Considerations:**
• Maximum time interval between doses should not exceed 12 hours
• Capsules should be swallowed whole with water
• Gabapentin is not indicated for postherpetic neuralgia in pediatric patients
• Use in pediatric patients less than 12 years with compromised renal function has not been studied; dose adjustments based on creatinine clearance are recommended for patients 12 years and older

**Discontinuation:** If discontinuing or reducing gabapentin, do so gradually over a minimum of 1 week.
